name: Flushed prefix versus late failure atomicity

payload.proof_obligation: If generations have been prewritten before a statement-level data error or suffix conflict, the transaction status and every recovery path must still force the whole logical statement to rollback.
payload.candidate_compiler: Intersect intermediate flush boundaries with ordinary later data errors, concurrent suffix writers, and irreversible status/recovery consumers. Require a log witness that at least one generation finished before the natural producer.
payload.reject_as_variant: Different row counts, key positions, SQL error strings, or flush thresholds under the same rollback-status owner.

provenance.introduced_for: turn concrete production schedules into reusable transaction fuzz cells

name: Pipelined DML keeps flushed prefixes atomic under late data errors and natural suffix conflicts

payload.production_workload: An autocommit INSERT/UPDATE/REPLACE workload explicitly selects tidb_dml_type=BULK, keeps metadata locking enabled, and exceeds the production flush gate of at least 16 MiB and 10000 mutation keys (or the 128 MiB force gate). Representative workloads are a large import with a late NULL, a bulk unique-key rewrite with a late duplicate, and an ordered upsert/import while an OLTP writer updates a suffix key.
payload.natural_producer: The input itself contains a bad row after a flushed prefix, or an ordinary concurrent OLTP transaction commits a key that the bulk statement has not yet prewritten. No network error or fabricated storage response is required.
ordering: late data error: generation_1_prewrite_done < evaluate_bad_suffix_row < SQL_error < rollback_status_publish
late conflict: bulk_start_ts < generation_1_prewrite_done < competitor_start_ts < competitor_commit_ts < generation_2_prewrite_suffix_key < write_conflict < rollback_status_publish
payload.defaults: MDL remained ON, autocommit remained ON, and the supported lazy-constraint path required by pipelined DML remained active. The only product opt-in was tidb_dml_type=BULK. Test-only failpoints reduced the 16 MiB/10000-key/128 MiB thresholds; they did not create the SQL error or write conflict.
payload.topology: Pinned current TiDB test process, one PD, and current nightly real TiKV 7ecce12. The proof is independent of replica failure and closes even in a single-Region topology.
payload.production_outcome: Late NOT NULL and duplicate errors returned errors and a fresh session saw no flushed prefix. A concurrent suffix writer committed, bulk DML returned error 9007, and a fresh session saw only the competitor row. ADMIN CHECK TABLE passed for every target. Successful REPLACE and ON DUPLICATE workloads matched standard DML row-for-row, including generated-column and unique-index state.
payload.control: Standard DML over the same ordered mutation stream matched BULK exactly. Removing the late bad row or concurrent suffix commit yields successful full apply; moving the competitor to an already prewritten key makes the competitor lose rather than allowing a hidden suffix conflict.
payload.holding_guard: Pipelined failure publishes rollback status for the transaction startTS; range cleanup removes flushed locks, and later readers can recover any residual rollback locks even if best-effort background cleanup is interrupted.
payload.reopen_only_if: A different failure can make the primary status commit, omit a logical prerequisite from recovery evidence, or return success/error with fresh durable rows that violate the standard-path result set.

provenance.introduced_for: require concrete production trigger before expanding a transaction candidate

evidence.not_null: generation 1 flushed 1024 keys before row 1500 returned error 1048; rollback resolved one Region; fresh count was zero
evidence.unique_update: 90 generations flushed 4551 row/index mutations before late duplicate; fresh key rows and sum matched the original state; ADMIN CHECK passed

matrix: 1500 ordered REPLACE rows crossing primary key and two unique-key owners
1800 ON DUPLICATE rows repeatedly rewriting the same 300 handles and generated-column index
evidence.oracle: standard and BULK sorted row sets were identical; ADMIN CHECK passed on all four tables

evidence.ordering: generation 1 prewrote 2048 keys at 17:28:09.676; competitor committed handle 1500 at commitTS 467670477081935875; generation 2 returned write conflict at 17:28:10.168
evidence.terminal: bulk statement returned error 9007 and did not retry
evidence.durable_truth: rollback range completed; fresh session saw only (1500,999999,online-winner); ADMIN CHECK passed

rationale: Late ordinary SQL errors and suffix write conflicts are covered by durable rollback status and read-assisted cleanup; reopen only above that recovery owner.
